help_step0_body:
PANDO automates the preparation of spatial data for creating travel demand models (e.g. for PTV Visum). For network planning purposes, the following standardised analysis methods are provided: (1) Identification of central places and intra-municipal centralities, (2) Network categorisation of road networks, (3) Accessibility analyses, and (4) Templates for travel demand models. The generation of traffic cells with population and structural data is based on multiple GIS operations executed as Python scripts using QGIS models. Subsequent analysis steps in PTV Visum are also automated: Reading the road network and traffic cells, generating connector access nodes, and running procedures for network categorisation and accessibility analyses.

Getting Started:

  • Proceed to Step 1: Location Search: Start a new project (enter location, download data, and define study area).
  • Open Existing Project: Load an existing PANDO project with all spatial data and computation states to resume or re-run processing.
  • Tip – Reusing Configurations & Parameters: In Step 3 (Grid) and Step 4 (QGIS Parameters), settings can be imported from another project at any time as a template.
  • Switch Language: Toggle between German and English at the top right.
help_step1_body:
Search for the centre of the model area via location search.

Features:

  • Search Location: Enter the name of a city or municipality and start search.
  • Found Locations: Select the correct location from search results.
  • Map Preview: Verify location and confirm centre point for the model.
  • Check on OSM.org: Link to view location on OpenStreetMap.org.
help_step2_body:
This step handles the selection and download of the required geodata.

Global Geodata (GHS-POP and GADM):

  • This data is downloaded once and remains available for future models.
  • Includes global population data (GHS-POP) and worldwide administrative units (GADM).

Select and Download OSM Regions:

  • OSM data is downloaded from Geofabrik using a built-in index to display and download selected regions.
  • The defined search radius (shown in blue on the map) determines the area for which available OSM data is searched and offered for download. This radius can be increased if additional data is required.
  • Entire countries (e.g. Germany) or individual parts (e.g. Baden-Württemberg) are available for download. Selecting a region that is already included in another selected region is not necessary.
  • Regions can be selected for download either by clicking the > button or by double-clicking the region name. The selection can be undone by clicking < or <<.

Download speed depends on your available internet connection. Once downloaded, data is ready for future projects without re-downloading. Please observe the privacy policies accepted at program start.
help_step3_body:
Define the spatial extent and level of detail of the model to be generated by defining the planning areas. The model consists of square grids of various resolutions for the four planning areas used in the model:

  • Planning Area (PA): The core study area with the highest level of detail. Edge length = b/9.
  • Influence Area 1 (IA1): Grid cells adjacent to the planning area with a slightly lower level of detail covering the immediate catchment area (edge length = b/3).
  • Influence Area 2 (IA2): The extended influence area. Edge length = b.
  • Outer Area (OA): Remaining model area, based on the OSM data selection defined in the previous step.

Grid Parameters:

These parameters affect the grid cells, which determines the size, number of cells, and level of detail in the model.

  • Edge length b [m]: Grid cell size in metres.
  • Radius [km]: Influences the displayed grid cells on the map that can then be assigned to the planning areas.
  • Load settings from another project: Use the 'Load grid settings from another project...' button to import cell size b and radius directly from an existing project configuration as a template without altering your current location.

Assign Planning Areas:

  • By selecting PA, IA1, or IA2, grid cells on the map can be assigned to a planning area. 'Select Cells' must be activated for map interaction. Selection is made by clicking or clicking and dragging. Clicking again removes the cell mark.
  • The 'Show generated traffic cells' option shows the borders of the resulting cells for subsequent model analysis.
  • The 'Generated Traffic Cells' box provides an overview of the traffic cells created by the selection. The total number only describes the number of grid cells. In the final model, cells for the outer area are also present as administrative traffic cell units.
help_step4_body:
This step handles the automated execution of the QGIS model chain and Osmium processing steps to generate traffic cells and structural data.

Load parameters from another project:

  • Use the 'Load parameters from another project...' button at the top right to import all model parameters (Model 2, Model 5, nationwide intensity) as well as reference data and census settings from another project as a template.

External Input Data for Population:

  • Custom population distribution data can be provided here.

Country-wide Intensity Estimation:

  • Selecting 'yes' generates an intensity estimation for the entire selected model area in the style of https://map.isv.uni-stuttgart.de/. This increases computation time.

Help and Tips:

  • Help and tips are visible by hovering the mouse over the input fields.
help_step5_body:
Automated loading of data into PTV Visum 2025 and execution of procedure steps.

Import of road network, import of traffic cells, generation of access nodes for connectors for network categorisation, connector generation, network categorisation execution, accessibility analysis execution, and loading graphic parameters. Results are saved in the project folder under '{visum_path}'. Further details follow on the next page.
help_step6_body:
Results and Evaluation:

Overview of SELECTED result data as well as short explanations of the data. Further documentation and explanations will follow in a new version of the tool.

  • 1. Base Data: Census population data and administrative boundaries (ADM0–ADM3).
  • 2. Central Places and Intra-Municipal Centralities: ADM2 central places, intensity estimation, POIs, and final traffic cells.
  • 3. Network Categorisation for Motorised Traffic: Categorised representation by OSM link types as well as RIN network categorisation and direct lines.
  • 4. Accessibility Analyses: Travel times to analysed destinations based on traffic cells.

Use the 'Open Folder', 'Open in QGIS', or 'Open in Visum' buttons to directly work with the data.
help_step7_body:
Results and Evaluation:

Overview of SELECTED result data as well as short explanations of the data. Further documentation and explanations will follow in a new version of the tool.

  • 1. Base Data: Census population data and administrative boundaries (ADM0–ADM3).
  • 2. Central Places and Intra-Municipal Centralities: ADM2 central places, intensity estimation, POIs, and final traffic cells.
  • 3. Network Categorisation for Motorised Traffic: Categorised representation by OSM link types as well as RIN network categorisation and direct lines.
  • 4. Accessibility Analyses: Travel times to analysed destinations based on traffic cells.

Use the 'Open Folder', 'Open in QGIS', or 'Open in Visum' buttons to directly work with the data.

step0_steps_group_title: The process consists of the following steps:
step0_urban_act_desc_body: Climate change and urbanization are two global developments transforming risks and opportunities in many regions worldwide, especially in the Asia-Pacific region. Many Asian cities face climate change impacts that pose risks to populations, ecosystems, and local economies. Urban-Act supports a transformation of urban development toward climate mitigation and resilience, focusing on cities in the Philippines, Thailand, India, China, and Indonesia.
step0_urban_act_goal_body: At the University of Stuttgart, the Institute of Spatial and Regional Planning (IREUS) and the Institute for Transport Studies (ISV) develop planning tools for integrated transport and land-use planning to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and enhance urban resilience.
step0_urban_act_group_title: This tool was developed as part of the Urban-Act project
step0_urban_act_links: Detailed project information is available at the International Climate Initiative (IKI) and Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. The project is funded by the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation, Nuclear Safety and Consumer Protection (BMUKN).
step0_urban_act_title: Urban-Act: Integrated Urban Climate Action for Low-Carbon and Resilient Cities
